speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate your newborn for feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting. Can you tell me the baby's age in hours or days, and whether they have passed any meconium stools yet?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: The baby is six hours old with bilious vomiting, which strongly suggests a distal intestinal obstruction rather than pyloric stenosis, given the bilious nature and early onset. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the abdomen shows a 'double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal X-ray showing a 'double bubble' sign is pathognomonic for duodenal atresia, which aligns perfectly with the bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance seen in this newborn. DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal atresia
